message.content:
Below is a quick‑look at the **long‑weekend** holidays that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that falls on a **Monday** or a **Friday**, giving you a three‑day break (Saturday – Sunday – holiday or holiday – Saturday – Sunday).

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-------|
| **Family Day** (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) | **Feb 20** | Monday | Creates a 3‑day break (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Good Friday** (all provinces) | **Apr 7** | Friday | Creates a 3‑day break (Fri‑Sat‑Sun). |
| **Victoria Day** (all provinces) | **May 22** | Monday | Creates a 3‑day break (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Labour Day** (all provinces) | **Sep 4** | Monday | Creates a 3‑day break (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Remembrance Day** (all provinces) | **Nov 11** | Monday | Creates a 3‑day break (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |
| **Christmas Day** (all provinces) | **Dec 25** | Monday | Creates a 3‑day break (Sat‑Sun‑Mon). |

> **Quick note:**  
> - **Canada Day** fell on Saturday, July 1, so it did *not* produce a long weekend.  
> - **Thanksgiving** (Oct 9) fell on Thursday, so it also did not create a long weekend.  
> - Some provinces have additional holidays that can create long weekends (e.g., Quebec’s St. Jean‑Baptiste on June 24, Friday). If you need province‑specific data, let me know!

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app. If you’d like a more detailed, province‑by‑province breakdown or additional holidays that might affect travel plans, just ask!
